clue.text: Be near front of sheep fold

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of the next word is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of sheep
to crimp is to press into small folds or ridges

explanation.surface: A shepherd is told to stand close to the front of the sheep pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near' here is the old sense of stingy, so 'Be near' is a verb phrase; 'fold' is not the pen but a pleat.
explanation.definitionFit: Near can mean mean or tight-fisted, and to scrimp is to be thrifty and economise hard.

clue.text: Dealt a last card, showing value of holding

indicators.note: cards that are dealt come out shuffled, so these letters are mixed

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A card player gets a final card and reveals the worth of the hand held.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' sounds like a hand of cards; it is a landholding.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadastral survey or register records land ownership, boundaries and assessed worth for taxation purposes.

clue.text: In a type of list

blocks.note: surface reading: included in some sort of inventory or register
setter's reading: list means lean, so this is a typeface that slopes to one side

explanation.walkthrough: A list is usually a catalogue, but a ship lists when it leans; a sloping typeface is one that leans.
explanation.definitionFit: This style of print slants to the right, so text set in it leans like a ship tilting over.

clue.text: Scheme to kidnap adult one of five in litter

indicators.note: kidnapping means seizing and holding someone, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: a plan is a scheme
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
a quin is one of quintuplets

explanation.surface: A plot to snatch a grown-up from a litter of five newborns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'litter' looks like the quintuplets' family; it means a carried chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A palanquin is a covered seat borne on poles by carriers, a kind of litter used in Asia.

clue.text: Well-built vehicle's in decline

indicators.note: 's stands for is, and being in something means sitting inside its letters

blocks.note: rot is decay or decline
a bus is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A sturdy-looking car or coach is nevertheless going downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: Robust describes something sturdy and strongly made, as a well-built person or object is.

clue.text: Show by mounted band?

blocks.note: rode is the past tense of ride, so mounted and travelled on a horse
O is a ring shape, a band

explanation.surface: A performance given by a group of musicians on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: A mounted band is surely a cavalry band; split it into a riding verb and a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is a public exhibition where cowboys display riding and roping skills, a kind of show.

clue.text: Black grease drops against end of court

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it go, so a letter is left out of the word

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
Vaseline is a brand of petroleum jelly, a grease
v is short for versus, meaning against

explanation.surface: A sticky dark lubricant spills onto the edge of a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: The baseline is the line marking the back limit of a tennis court, at either end.

clue.text: Exploit dwarf

blocks.note: first meaning: a daring feat or trick
second meaning: to stop something from growing

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as taking advantage of a small person, but both words have other senses: a feat, and to hold back growth.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a showy daring feat and, as a verb, to check or restrict growth.

clue.text: Rush around barrier, or duck

blocks.note: to gad about is to rush around restlessly
a wall is a barrier

explanation.surface: Instructions for getting past a wall: run round it or crouch down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' looks like a verb, a choice beside rushing round; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The gadwall is a greyish dabbling species of wild duck found across Europe and North America.

clue.text: Manipulate lines in German with the appropriate article

indicators.note: something in another sits inside it, so these letters are placed within the next word

blocks.note: the first part of German
RY is short for railway, lines of track
the rest of German
der is one form of the German word for the, apt after German

explanation.surface: A language lesson on choosing the correct grammatical gender in German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lines' looks like part of the definition only; it is also the railway inside GERMAN. Der is a German definite article, so 'appropriate' to the language.
explanation.definitionFit: To gerrymander is to redraw electoral boundaries unfairly for party advantage, so it is rigging constituency lines.

clue.text: Backtracks in attempt to cause trouble

indicators.note: one item sits in the other, so its letters are placed inside
the word opens with back, telling us the combined letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: a bid is an attempt
ruts are tracks worn in the ground

explanation.surface: Someone retraces their steps in a bid to stir things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backtracks' looks like one verb but does two jobs: its first half signals the turnaround and its second half supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To disturb is to interrupt or agitate, which is causing trouble or upset.

clue.text: One who earns drink holds promotion closer to heart

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a brew is a drink, of tea or beer
an ad is an advertisement, a promotion
inner means nearer the centre

explanation.surface: A worker's pint embraces a career advance that matters deeply.
explanation.definitionFit: The breadwinner is the person whose wages support a household, the family's main earner.

clue.text: In which one wants an empty chamber

definitions.text: In which one wants an empty chamber

blocks.clueFragment: In which one wants an empty chamber
blocks.note: surface reading: a situation where someone hopes for a vacant room
setter's reading: the chamber of a revolver with one bullet loaded, where each player hopes the next pull finds no round

explanation.walkthrough: A chamber sounds like a room to be let; it is the cylinder slot of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: In this deadly game of chance a player spins a revolver's cylinder and fires, survival depending on an unloaded slot.

clue.text: This has three feet and an arm

blocks.note: first meaning: the imperial length of three feet
second meaning: a spar across a ship's mast, whose end is the yardarm

explanation.walkthrough: Three feet and an arm suggest some odd creature; they are a measurement and a piece of rigging.
explanation.definitionFit: The imperial unit equals thirty-six inches, and on a sailing ship the same word names the horizontal spar holding a sail.

clue.text: Fool them out and about

indicators.note: turned about suggests the preceding letters are moved around into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An order to throw some idiot out and away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the letters; 'about' does the stirring.
explanation.definitionFit: A muttonhead is an informal insult for a dull, stupid person, the same as a fool.

clue.text: New doctor/patient relationship's shaky

indicators.note: something new has been remade, so the letters take a fresh order

blocks.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fledgling bond between a physician and someone in their care is on wobbly ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Trepidant is a rare adjective meaning trembling or quaking with fear, so shaky and nervous.

clue.text: Cities got sacked in vain

indicators.note: a sacked city is plundered and wrecked, so its letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Towns were plundered, but all to no purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in vain' looks like a phrase meaning uselessly; 'in' is only a link and 'vain' means conceited.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone egotistic is self-centred and conceited, thinking too highly of themselves, which is being vain.

clue.text: One under this is thought unlucky

definitions.text: One under this is thought unlucky

blocks.clueFragment: One under this is thought unlucky
blocks.note: surface reading: anyone living beneath some sign or star is ill-fated
setter's reading: the number one less than this is the superstitiously unlucky thirteen

explanation.walkthrough: 'One under' suggests a person under a curse; it is the number one below.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirteen is the traditionally unlucky number, and it sits immediately below the answer in counting.

clue.text: Bats over fields - that's one's game

definitions.text: Bats over fields - that's one's game

blocks.note: surface reading: flying bats flitting across meadows
setter's reading: a cricketer who bats, plays overs and fields, doing every part of the game

explanation.walkthrough: Bats, over and fields are all cricket words; an over is a set of six balls bowled. The answer's second half also hints at the game of rounders.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-rounder is a cricketer skilled at both batting and bowling, contributing to every department of play.

clue.text: Norse god is said to be restrained

indicators.note: said means we are to go by the spoken sound of the next word

blocks.note: low-key means restrained or understated

explanation.surface: A claim that a certain Scandinavian deity keeps himself in check.
explanation.definitionFit: Loki is the shape-shifting trickster figure among the gods of Norse mythology.

clue.text: Joint game, if back first

blocks.note: first meaning: a cured leg of pork, a joint of meat
second meaning: put back in front of it and you get the board game backgammon

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is cryptic: the word becomes a game when back is put before it. A gammon is also a win in backgammon.
explanation.definitionFit: Gammon is a cured ham joint, and preceding it with back names a familiar dice-and-board game.

clue.text: Those submerging one story with a variation

indicators.note: a variation is a changed version, so the letters of the story and a are altered in order

blocks.note: divers are people who go under water
I is the Roman numeral one
fiction is a made-up story
taken as written

explanation.surface: Scuba divers telling a tale with a twist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variation' does double duty: it shuffles the story plus a, and also defines the whole answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Diversification is the act of making things varied, introducing variety into a range or portfolio.

clue.text: Dean eats 5 from part of shell

indicators.note: something that eats takes food inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a dean or dene is a narrow valley, a vale
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A college dean eats part of a crab or oyster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dean' looks like the college official; it is the old word for a wooded valley. '5' looks like a cross-reference to another clue but is simply a number.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the two hinged halves of a bivalve mollusc's casing is called a valve.

clue.text: Perfect for a trade

blocks.note: a means one, and I is the Roman numeral one
a deal is a trade or transaction

explanation.surface: Something is just right for a particular line of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective describes something that is the best possible, exactly what perfect means.

clue.text: Go through again to take point with ease

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: to relive an experience is to go through it again
E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: Revisiting a painful episode so as to make a point more comfortably.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve pain or worry is to lessen it, which is to ease it.

clue.text: Reader of current issue?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone who buys the latest edition of a magazine
setter's reading: an instrument that gives a reading of the electric current flowing

explanation.walkthrough: A reader of the current issue sounds like a magazine subscriber; the reader is a meter, the current electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: This instrument measures electric current in amperes, its dial displaying the value as a reading.

clue.text: Part of boat protecting sailors inside shell

indicators.note: something protecting another wraps round it, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: the keel is the backbone along a boat's bottom
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: The hull of a boat shields the crew inside its outer casing.
explanation.definitionFit: A kernel is the edible seed found within the hard casing of a nut, the part in a shell.

clue.text: 10-1 it's a good combination

blocks.note: the number written in words
an ace counts as one in cards

explanation.surface: Betting odds of ten to one are a winning mix.
explanation.walkthrough: 10-1 reads as odds; split it into a ten and an ace, both cards.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, a tenace is a holding of two high cards ranked one apart with a gap, a strong combination for finessing.
